english_verification.review_scope: Checked representative current Mod opening history, English names, shared G52/G00 mission scope, Laskaris and crisis event context, republican mechanics, and the actual fixed-revision Ameion, Two Heroes, and Kheionism Wiki passages; not an exhaustive mission, disaster, or AI audit. Native English national-idea names and descriptions were compared by localisation key by the primary. Large source intervals are locator envelopes, not a claim to inspect every intervening line or establish complete runtime reachability.
unresolved: Wiki historical timelines and lore do not certify current mission rewards, disaster severity, or the reachability of every route.
G00 is an optional civil-war continuation and J99 is an optional mission-tree detour; neither is a simple successor fact for every campaign.
Inherited percentage displays and unit interpretations remain source values and were not recalculated.

rationale.campaign_length: 55 direct missions span early conquest, mid-game integration, late archaeology, and imperial crisis, making this a long campaign.
rationale.colonization: Devand, Chandya, and Iphilé include settlement, border arrangements, and jungle frontiers, but this is not a conventional overseas coloniser.
rationale.complexity: War, subjects, culture and religion, political sliders, archaeology, and disasters run in parallel and demand careful timing and resources.
rationale.dark_story: The civilisational revival includes forced assimilation, labour, land seizure, and civil war, but does not aim at indiscriminate destruction.
rationale.difficulty: A powerful opening lowers survival difficulty, while monarch-point pressure, multi-front wars, and the late civil war raise completion difficulty.
rationale.diplomacy: The Eucanthe alliance, Kheionai city-states, Muteba, and multiple subject types require long-term relation and liberty-desire management.
rationale.early_pressure: Laskaris is extremely strong, but his limited lifespan and mission tempo encourage constant war; playing slowly wastes the advantage.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Precursor archaeology, ruins, Tasheni, magical wood, and special ships form a complete technological exploration line.
rationale.narrative_density: The prophetic death date, two heroes, succession crisis, civilisational programme, archaeological obsession, and monarchist civil war form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: Cities, local capitals, ruins, and Tasheni matter, but serve a continental empire rather than a purely tall campaign.
rationale.trade_economy: Sea power, ports, free ports, and east-west trade support the imperial treasury without displacing war and governance.
rationale.warfare: Laskaris's countdown, Taychend's unification, regional hegemony, and civil war demand continuous and ever larger wars.

identity.appearance: An Ambhen Kheionist republic in 1444; the monarchist civil war can switch the player to G00 Nákyra while continuing the same mission tree.

successors.relationship: An optional player faction in the late monarchist civil war; it shares all 55 missions with G52 and continues the same campaign chain after victory.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
For a long time Ameion was in isolation, focused on building a worthy capital and slowly colonizing its surroundings. In that age, we were nothing more than a peripheral state; forgotten to the world.

This all changed with the rise of Laskaris, a mighty elf and a brilliant speaker, who learned the time of his demise, effectively giving him immortality before his deathday. Using this, he got himself elected and became the leader of Ameion. He renovated the army and navy, and led them on a path of conquest through Taychend; his ultimate goal being the seizure of the jewel of Taychend, the great city of Nanru Nakar, Nákyra in Kheionai.

His victories gave us a presence in Taychend, but there is still much to be done. Even now, rebels and warlords conspire against us; threatening to push us back into the sea. But this will never occur, for one day Laskaris’ dream will be realized, and all of Taychend will fall under our dominion.

description.text:
Many centuries ago a movement grew among the Nékheis, conspiring to kick out their Alecandi overlords and establish a great kingdom of cities in Devand. The subsequent war that followed would see these heroes defeated, chased to the edge of the known world. Tired and exhausted, they finally settled down near where a great river emptied into the sea, and this settlement would eventually grow into a grand city; known to us as Ameion.

At last, we re-established contact with our cousins to the west. Although much bad blood remains between us, it is prudent that we mend these old wounds. Our diplomats have been slowly but steadily restoring ties with the other Kheions, learning many tricks to appease their leaders in the process.

description.text:
The Taychendi are an odd people, so similar, yet so distinct from our own. They live in city states, yet bend the knee to monarchs. They practice agriculture, yet also feel the need to raid eachother’s lands constantly. They produce great philosophers and writers, yet worship dead rulers as gods.

Their history is tragic, a constant cycle of conflict, consolidation, and collapse; repeating continuously since the Erriphi and bringing only suffering and chaos in its wake. As far as the Taychendi are concerned, we are merely the next in a long series of conquerors seeking to rule Taychend.

Our philosophers have determined that it is the Taychendi belief system, that of god-heroes and divine kings, that is the source of Taychend’s misery. We will institute a great program to "Kheionize" the Taychendi. By education, policies, and intermarriage, the Taychendi will become properly civilized; and the cycle of warlordism will meet its end under Kheionai guidance.

description.text: One of the policies introduced to further the Kheionization of the Taychendi was the Fotistrépei System. Taychendi soldiers serving in the Ameioni army, who willingly adopted Kheionai culture and became Kheionized, would receive land and privileges from Ambhen administrators; which were often seized from disloyal Taychendi nobility and peasantry. These soldiers, known as Fotistrépei, formed a permanent and loyal native force, whose existence and status was tied to the success of the Ameioni Empire. The Fotistrépei would form one of the core groups of the emerging Klereyen culture that developed in the 1500s and were instrumental in the rise of the Klereyen within Ameioni society.

description.text:
In the years following the exile of our ancestors, they underwent numerous hardships building a society from nothingness. They were forced to create a functioning and stable state with what few resources they had and, unlike the Nékheis, had no aid from our cousins to the west.

Of the systems that developed during this dark period of isolation, Eisphoráth was the harshest. Disregarding its strictness, it was a well run and advanced system of labor and resource management, invented to ensure all contributed their dues to ensure the survival of the settlement. This system was abandoned over time, as the need for it disappeared with the reestablishment of trade links to the rest of the world.

As our consolidation of Taychend continues, many of our officials have begun to look to the past for inspiration to solve our current issues with the Taychendi not cooperating. It is about time we reintroduce the Eisphoráth, for only with a harsh system like this will the Taychendi be coerced into properly contributing to our empire.

description.text: The Ýmytolí are a series of fortifications created to repress the ever present rebels that hide among the various hills of Taychend. Built in strategic positions that not only offer great defensiveness but also easy access to supply lines and reinforcements, the Ýmytolí are always kept in perfect condition.

description.text:
At first there were few. A small group of ships, explorers from a faraway continent beyond Aelantir. But this trickle turned into a flood, as all sorts of foreign people of differing colors and sizes crowded our Taychendi ports, seeking to steal the valuable relics of our ancestors.

At first, they were tolerated. But soon, our local administrators placed restrictions on their movement and influence. Once our agents learned of Cannorian companies supplying Taychendi rebellions against us, the decision was clear. The Cannorians were barred from our ports for good and we sent our fleet to stop the Cannorians from ever reaching Taychendi shores. Unfortunately, the Cannorian greed for ancient elven relics was so great, that smugglers soon appeared to meet their demand…

We face a constant struggle against the Cannorians, who seek to bring down our empire to satisfy their greed. We will not let their wishes be realized for we are inheritors of the Precursor legacy; and we will not let the foreigners defile it.

description.text:
Laskaris the conqueror came to Taychend in a great effort to bring the benefits of civilization. His heroic actions saved them from the barbarity and warlordism they were so accustomed to. Since his prophesized passing, a cult grew around the worship of him and his descendants among the Taychendi, who see him and his bloodline as divine. And among those that did not see his bloodline as divine, they certainly venerated the principles Laskaris and his descendants would espouse: populism.

Thirendires, a descendant of Laskaris, would rise to power with the support of the Laskarian cult and the common people behind him. He ascended to kingship, proclaiming that the people have elected the bloodline of Laskaris as the rulers of these lands. The great rebellion that followed by those still believing in the philosophized ideal of a republic was crushed, and Thirendires proclaimed a new populist and Monarchist era for the world of the Kheionai.

description.text: The large archeological program conducted by the Nákyran Empire led to the rediscovery of ancient Precursor building techniques and styles, which the Laskaris dynasty embraced wholeheartedly as the new official building style of the empire. A large building spree would ensue, with every city in every region of the empire having constant construction projects built in the precursor style and old buildings being renovated to emulate them.

description.text: The Klereyen are the Taychendi that have embraced civizilation and the ways of the Kheionai. Even still, they were not properly integrated into the government of Ameion. This changed with the ascension of Thirendires to kingship, with the Klereyen as his most loyal followers. He rewarded them by putting them in the highest levels of administration and favoring them as such. In every part of the empire of Nákyra, the Klereyen can be found, a policy continued by Thirendires's successors, who saw the Klereyen as their most loyal base of support.

description.text:
Even after their defeat on the field of battle, many Kheionai still cling to their philosophized ideal of a republic. While many among them are too disheartened to continue resistance, many more refuse to acknowledge, and actively resist the truth: the blood of Laskaris are the rulers of these lands. The lingering resentment and occasional rebellion against the monarchy has led to the need to create a new force designed specifically to combat this ever present threat: The Krypharpedan.

Recruited from amongst the most loyal of Klereyen, they actively hunt the republican resistance. Especially active in the Devand and in the kheions, they are the shield that keeps the royal family, and Nákyra as a whole, safe from both domestic and foreign attack.

Once our agents learned of Cannorian companies supplying Taychendi rebellions against us, the decision was clear. The Cannorians were barred from our ports for good and we sent our fleet to stop the Cannorians from ever reaching Taychendi shores. Unfortunately, the Cannorian greed for ancient elven relics was so great, that smugglers soon appeared to meet their demand…

We face a constant struggle against the Cannorians, who seek to bring down our empire to satisfy their greed. We will not let their wishes be realized for we are inheritors of the Precursor legacy; and we will not let the foreigners defile it.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you dislike time pressure, scarce monarch points, cultural assimilation, long multi-front wars, or an imperial protagonist.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Use a super-ruler for rapid conquest early, manage subjects, assimilation, cities, and archaeology in the middle game, then expand in several directions and reserve money, manpower, and forts for the G52–G00 continental civil war.
player_overview.overview: You are the easternmost republic of the Kheionai world, ruled at the start by the nearly unbeatable Laskaris before his destined death. Conquer Taychend quickly, turn allies, city-states, and conquered peoples into subjects and Kheionised society, and invest in Precursor archaeology; later expand across South Aelantir and choose a side when republican and monarchist forces split the empire. The story is dense and the systems are numerous, but its civilisational revival rests on coercive assimilation and high-pressure rule.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy Alexander-like conquest, strong-character narratives, republican politics, subject management, archaeology, and major disasters.
signature_features: Laskaris is overwhelmingly powerful before his prophetic death date, forcing the player to turn a personal legend into state foundations through continuous war.
Republican politics, autonomous city-states, and a subject network coexist with Kheionisation, military settlement, and centralisation; governance choices shape the empire.
Precursor archaeology and the search for Tasheni lead into the late continental civil war, making the strongest empire fight over its legitimacy.
player_overview.tagline: Follow a conqueror who knows his death date and use a republic, legions, subjects, and Precursor ruins to impose an atheistic imperial order on South Aelantir.

reasons: Laskaris's prophetic death date turns a strong-character story into an early tempo mechanic.
Subjects, autonomy, culture, and religious integration add layers beyond ordinary map-painting.
Archaeology and the lost floating city provide long-term investment goals independent of war.
The late G52–G00 civil war tests the empire's institutions at its moment of greatest strength.
warnings: Rapid conquest and complicated prerequisites create a clear timetable.
Archaeology, technology, stability, and expansion all compete for monarch points.
Late disasters can split the realm and subjects; blind play has little margin for error.
The national story includes forced assimilation, labour, and civilisational supremacism.

values.rationale: Kheionisation, cultural and religious assimilation, and the imperial civilisational mission first produce a more uniform society; land seizure, labour, and coercive transformation further reduce the value score, while the state also provides city-building, stability, limited autonomy, and avenues of advancement. Imperial expansion itself is not counted twice as evidence of evil.
